verdict.rationale: Better Auth documents defining roles and permissions through its organization plugin and managing user roles through its admin plugin, and a community user confirms it offers RBAC. However, the evidence never shows how those permissions are enforced in authorization checks, nor that roles are surfaced in session tokens or JWT claims; the JWT plugin is documented only for issuing and verifying tokens. Missing for 10: documented permission-check enforcement API, evidence that roles/permissions appear in session or JWT tokens, hands-on corroboration of RBAC enforcement.

support.subject: As a developer, I can define roles and permissions and have them enforced and surfaced in session tokens for authorization checks

citations.quote: Organizations simplifies user access and permissions management. Assign roles and permissions to streamline project management, team coordination, and partnerships.
It allows administrators to perform various operations such as creating users, managing user roles, banning/unbanning users, impersonating users, and more.
Multi-tenancy built in. Teams, roles, invitations, and access control.
A commenter said it does far more than next-auth/auth.js: authn/z, acting as an identity provider and OIDC/SSO provider, RBAC, and SAML/SCIM.
